result.title: Visual Thinking: Training-Free Active Perception for Counting and Localizing Hard-to-Find Objects
result.summary: Vision foundation models can precisely segment objects based solely on a text prompt. However, they struggle to recover objects that are small, occluded or whose appearance is poorly captured by the original textual description. Vision language models can examine the image and its context, they can propose richer descriptions of the objects to be detected. But these models struggle with precise segmentation and localization. We introduce Visual Thinking, a training-free framework that combines a vision-language model with Segment Anything Model 3 (SAM 3) through an iterative active perception loop. At each iteration, the VLM proposes short noun phrases using the image, candidate crops and history from past iterations. A controller ranks these phrases using embedding similarity between the original prompt and the proposal, an entropy-based verification priority and the novelty of the prompt. Next, SAM 3 uses prompts to detect objects in the image. We associate detections across iterations and update each object's confidence score using a weighted mean of scores obtained from SAM 3 with a larger weight for detections using narrower prompts. We supply confident detections as positive visual exemplars for SAM 3, and incorporate image tiling to recover small objects in cluttered images. We evaluate counting and localization on CARPK, FSCD-147, PixMo-Count, and OmniCount (Fruits). Compared with SAM 3, Visual Thinking reduces the counting mean absolute error (MAE) by about 18 on FSC-147 and about 8 on CARPK. It improves box average precision (AP) by more than 12 on FSCD-147 and CARPK. Visual Thinking, with fixed or no tiling, performs on par with Claude Opus 5.5 at extra-high reasoning effort, while running on single desktop GPU in about 5.91 seconds per image, compared to about 46.53 seconds per image for Claude through its API.

AI.brief_summary: 提出免训练的「Visual Thinking」框架：VLM 在多轮主动感知循环中依据原图、候选裁剪和历史生成短语查询，由基于相似度、熵优先与新意的控制器排序后驱动 SAM 3 检测，并用跨轮关联、置信度加权、正例提示与图像切块提升难找物体的计数与定位。
AI.relevance_reason: 该工作把「看哪里、用什么描述取证据、证据如何累积」外化为显式循环，其短语排序、熵驱动的验证优先与跨轮置信度更新，可供核查 LVR 中视觉证据筛选与 THINK/LOOK/STOP 成本收益的对应关系；但其推理状态外在于语言与检测器，而非模型内部 latent，需区分。
